Receivables Reporting Pack

Turns the monthly AR bridge and overdue exports into a reconciled KPI scorecard, an AR bridge, cluster charts and a customer table — then generates the Excel master workbook, the PowerPoint deck and an email draft with both attached.

Open demo

The original is an internal tool and is not linked here. The demo is a redacted copy: company name, logo, brand colours, customer codes and internal process settings were removed, and it loads generated sample workbooks with invented customers and amounts.

The problem

Month-end receivables reporting meant rebuilding the same workbook and slide deck by hand from system exports: matching customers across periods and files, reconciling balances, and re-keying figures into tables and charts.

What it does

  • Reads .xlsx workbooks in the browser and finds the right columns by scoring header names, so changed headings or column order do not break it; the period is inferred from headers and sheet names.
  • Reconciliation checks: the AR roll-forward (beginning + sales + collections + offsets = ending), duplicate codes, customers missing from a period or from the overdue file, and low-confidence column matches.
  • KPI scorecard comparing the month with the same month last year, with the favourable or unfavourable direction stated for each measure.
  • AR bridge (waterfall) for the whole portfolio or any single customer, cluster charts for sales, collections, receivables and overdue amounts, and a searchable customer table.
  • Generates an Excel master workbook with formulas and native charts (11 sheets), a 12-slide PowerPoint deck with native charts, and an .eml email draft with both files attached.
  • Column mapping and cluster reclassification can be overridden in the page and are remembered in the browser.
